scope: Read-only current S3 age presentation and its caller/tests; JVM consent disk roundtrip and static preference wiring only.

findings.problem: The existing select familyAge grammar accepts only a bare numeric family age. Later confirmed family statements with negation or a Jahre-alt suffix fall back to generic claim with holder Meine Tochter Klara instead of Klara, so they do not participate in the named persons ledger conflict/revocation decision. The new exactAgeReply can therefore display the older29 as an exact age.
regression_pairs: Meine Tochter Klara ist 30 Jahre alt.
findings.expected: Negation must suppress the old exact value; newer supported family age must yield30 or abstain, and revocation of that newer family statement must not resurrect29.
findings.smallest_repair_direction: Retain same-holder unsupported/negated family statements as invalidators, or use a bounded shared family-holder grammar and fail closed when the remainder cannot supply a supported exact age. Do not broaden unsupported statements into answers.

other_checks.provenance: select requires genuine confirmed owner records; exactAgeReply requires unique ledger ID and byte-identical ranked content/kind. LearningExperience validates content hash and ID.
other_checks.mutation: New helper only reads records; no owner-fact or model write introduced. Existing dialogue-history save remains.
other_checks.age_semantics: Owner-statement age explicitly distinguished from automatically advanced current age.
other_checks.disk_test: Explicit JVM file roundtrip of mode string into fresh policy/gate; no Android SharedPreferences or device E2E claim.
other_checks.static_wiring: Actual restoredMode caller and preferences read/commit/setMode checks present.
